data.long_meaning: The name Bernice is of Hebrew-Greek origin, derived from the Hebrew name Bernice, meaning 'son of strength' or 'son of the strong one'. In Greek, Bernice is also associated with the name Bernice of Cyzicus, a Christian saint and martyr who lived in the 3rd century. The name Bernice is therefore significant in Christian tradition as a reminder of strength and resilience in the face of adversity.

data.etymology: Bernice belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bearer of strength.”

in_hebrew.name: ברניס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ברניס (ברניס) היא שם מלכים ביוונית. מקורו במלכה ביווניה, הנקראת ברניקה (Βερνίκη). השם עולה בספר מקבי א' (1:11). משמעותו: 'מלכה של כבוד', 'כבוד המלכה'.

in_greek.name: Βερνίκη
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Βερνίκη (Βερνίκη) είναι το ελληνικό όνομα μιας βασιλίσσας της Μακεδονίας. Εμφανίζεται στο Β' Μακκαβαϊκό (1:11). Σημαίνει: 'Βασιλίσσα των τιμών', 'Τιμή της Βασίλισσας'.

in_latin.name: Bernice
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Berniciae, originem habet a regina Graeciae, Bernica. In libro 1 Maccabaeorum (1:11) apparet. Significatio: 'Rex honorum', 'Honores regis'.

in_english.name: Bernice
in_english.meaning: Queen of honor, princess of reverence, or noble woman
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bernice is derived from the Greek name Βερνίκη (Bernikē), which refers to the queen of Greece, Bernica. It is mentioned in the 1 Maccabees (1:11) and means 'Queen of honor' or 'Princess of reverence'. In Christian tradition, the name Bernice is associated with the biblical figure Bernice, the daughter of King Herod Agrippa I, who is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles (25:13).

biblical_reference.note: Bernice, daughter of King Herod Agrippa I, appears in the Acts of the Apostles (25:13) as a witness to the trial of Paul the Apostle.

historical_references.reference: Bernice was an early Christian martyr who lived in the 3rd century AD and was venerated in North Africa. She was a wealthy woman who converted to Christianity and was persecuted for her faith. According to legend, she was subjected to various tortures, including being exposed to the elements and burned at the stake, but she remained steadfast in her faith and was eventually beheaded. Bernice is now remembered as a patron saint of converts and those suffering from persecution.
historical_references.context: Early Christian persecution in North Africa

historical_references.reference: Bernice of Clermont (c. 410–c. 449 AD) was a Christian bishop and abbess in Gaul. She is best known for her role in the establishment of the monastery at Sainte-Croix in Clermont, where she served as abbess. Bernice was also a noted ascetic and writer, and her correspondences with other religious figures, such as Saint Jerome, provide valuable insights into the spiritual practices and beliefs of early Christian communities.
historical_references.context: Establishment and growth of monasteries and ascetic practices in early Christian Gaul
